name: Sudraka
bio: Sudraka (Shudraka) is the name traditionally given to the author of the Sanskrit play The Little Clay Cart (Mrcchakatika). Nothing reliable is known of him: the play's own prologue calls him a king, learned in the Vedas and the lore of elephants, who lived to a hundred years and ten days and then entered the fire, but this is generally taken as legend, and scholars date the work anywhere from about the 3rd to the 5th century.

The Little Clay Cart, in ten acts, is unusual among Sanskrit dramas for its setting among merchants, courtesans, gamblers and thieves of the city of Ujjayini rather than among gods and kings. It tells of the love of the impoverished Brahman merchant Charudatta for the courtesan Vasantasena, and of the villainous Sansthanaka, who brings a false charge of murder against him. It is read here in Arthur W. Ryder's English prose and verse of 1905.
